# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Supplementary design document**. This document supplements
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md),
> expanding the RFC's phase sequence into **independently committable and independently verifiable**
> three-level tasks.
>
> The phase order and acceptance gates are governed solely by the main text of RFC-039. This
> document is responsible only for decomposing the work to an executable granularity and recording
> conflicts that still require adjudication.

## Positioning and Scope

| Level       | Count       | Meaning                                                                                          |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10) | Phases, in one-to-one correspondence with the phase sequence in RFC-039                          |
| **Level 2** | 73          | Task groups: work groups decomposed by phase, each able to be staffed and archived independently |
| **Level 3** | 268         | Units of work that can be committed and verified independently                                   |

**Numbering gaps (not reused)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`; after the LALRPOP route
was withdrawn, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` were also left unused (2026-11-25). All three have had no
corresponding entries since the WBS was established—the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1`
have zero matches in the entire history of this document
(`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md` can be used to verify this),
and there are no repository-wide references to them. `8.1` corresponds precisely to phase 1 of `05`
(test revival and completion): that phase was split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so P8's
numbering aligns with its phase number (phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so forth).

**Covered by this document**: Task decomposition, dependencies, parallelization groups, and binding
acceptance criteria.

**Not covered by this document**: The design rationale for individual tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the
rationale for phase ordering (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: Newly registered level-2/level-3 rows **must
contain two fields**—"**owning phase**" (the P to which the task actually belongs, which may differ
from the section containing it) and "**blocks the mainline**"; `awaiting scheduling` is no longer
the default state, and an omitted field means **not schedulable**. Numbers must be **unique across
the entire document** (tasks on other tracks use a track number, such as `029g.x`, and must not
occupy `N.x`).

**Closure registration (effective 2026-11-24)**: A checked row contains only four items—the task id,
status, **implementation commit short hash** (7 digits), and issue number, if any—written on one
line: `- [x] **3.24.1 Remaining pattern-matching completion items** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. **Do
not record the fix, criterion chain, gate thresholds, file line numbers, test names, or review
conclusions**: those belong in the commit message (`git show <short-hash>`). This table is a board,
not a process chronicle. **Do not record adjudication labels or restate conclusions**: "user
decision A/B/C", "option A", "the final implementation is…" and similar wording must not appear in
this table—the board answers only "is it complete?"; consult the commit message and the RFC-039
decision register for adjudications and results.

**The short hash is determined after the push**: a closure row records the short hash on
`origin/dev` after the push is complete; the order is **push the implementation commit first, then
write the closure row** (see “Commit hash is obtained after push” in
[commit-convention](../commit-convention.md)). The closure commit itself carries no
hash—self-reference is impossible.

**The count column contains only numbers**: the level-1/level-2/level-3 counts under
`Positioning and Scope` contain only the current values; increment/decrement histories such as
`+1 = …` do not belong in the table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “implementation points” from eight documents into the main table, **five
hard gaps in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been resolved:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Resolution                                                                                                                                             |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| G1  | **P5 has no implementation steps whatsoever**. RFC-039 defines P5 (splitting the checker) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents contains a section describing how to perform the split; `annotations.rs` appears once in the directory tree in `01-routing.md` and is the only mention in the entire batch                                                                                          | The P5 steps are supplied by this document (see below)                                                                                                 |
| G2  | **The three ownership claims for the `include!` transformation have no landed implementation**. RFC-039 places it in P4; `02` assigns the reference to itself; S7 in `06` also lists it. However, the change list in `02` (6 additions + 20 modifications) contains **no `semantic_tokens.rs`**                                                                                                                                            | The implementation steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 below (after P4 is complete); the references in RFC-039 and `06` have been synchronized to point here |
| G3  | **Three coexisting lists of CI scripts**. `RFC` lists four `scripts/ci/*.py` scripts; `01` lists four scripts + 1 `cargo test`; `07` lists four different checks (all with different names); `04` also previously listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (that script was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication, there are **at least 9 new scripts and no unified list**; `check-obligations.py` is owned by both P4 and P9 | The unified list appears in §P9 below (10 active scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents must refer to that table                       |
| G4  | **Conflict over the life or death of `precedence_inline.rs`**. `06` counts it among the “1,005 lines that must be revived,” while B6 in the same document says it “must be deleted together with the `Precedence` enum”; `05` advocates deletion                                                                                                                                                                                           | **Revive in P1, retain in P8** (decision registered as C1; Pratt is no longer to be deleted)                                                           |
| G5  | **Conflicting wording for the L2 target**: RFC-039 and the index in this directory previously said “grammar-driven syntax”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | This has converged on a **declarative precedence table + an unambiguous language surface** ([05](05-frontend-paradigm.md) §Grammar), see P8 8.3        |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: The three prohibitions—no fabrication, no endless filling, and no
patching when a refactor is required—constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be established
before work begins; otherwise, P1 would already be adding `mod` declarations to `tests/mod.rs` while
reviving tests, which is precisely the source of the G4 conflict.

### P3 Correctness Defects (Minimal Fix)

Source: Defect-fix half of [02](02-stage-contract.md) §Implementation Points S3 ＋
**Silent-Discard-Point Audit of 2026-10-07 (3.4)**

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, user decision of 2026-10-11)**: If this track or a later phase
> discovers a defect for which the “old behavior does not count as success”—**A silent failure / B
> silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and uncontrolled resource usage** (crash, stack exhaustion,
> or silently returning the wrong answer)—it **may be fixed along the way**, but all four
> requirements must be met: ① red first, then green (the red criterion must exist first and must
> genuinely fail); ② do not change the externally observable behavior of programs that “previously
> compiled successfully and ran correctly” (they must not start failing, and their existing
> diagnostic codes/text/exit codes must not be removed or changed); ③ register it in the same commit
> (this row annotates the error type + that phase's revision note + the PR mandatory block line
> “error type”); ④ regenerate the baseline in the same commit + manually review the diff. **D
> user-visible semantics / E external contract table / F RFC-level design changes must still receive
> prior adjudication. See [07 §Routing Criteria for Semantic Corrections](07-equivalence-oracle.md)
> for the expanded criteria and A–F whitelist;** the approach of “default super-refactor +
> after-the-fact registration” is **not adopted** (rationale: see RFC-039 D59: without a red
> criterion, there is no way to distinguish a fix from a regression, and this conflicts with both
> “there is no C5′” and “no relaxation of any kind”).

**Acceptance**: The defect criteria turn green, and **deliberately removing the fix must make them
turn red again**. **Risk**: The new E4018 on the multi-file path is a breaking change.

**3.4 acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must have red criteria first (changing code first is prohibited);
3.4.3 is a manual review; 3.4.4–3.4.8 are governed by C2/C3 and the P9 9.2 gate. **Risk**: The new
diagnostic in 3.4.1 is a behavior change and requires synchronized corpus differential baseline and
CHANGELOG updates.

> **Stop-the-bleeding channel**: P3 need not wait for all of P2. The only hard prerequisites for
> 3.1/3.2 are **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus layer) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two red criteria)**;
> 2.1/2.2/2.3.1/2.3.3 (IR verifier, snapshots, single-file differential, performance baseline) may
> proceed in parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding from correctness defects (such as `Sorted(3)`
> silently passing) must not be blocked by snapshot infrastructure. 3.3 (panic to diagnostic) has no
> prerequisite and may land at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted 2026-10-02;
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactor itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by an
ordering constraint.** It is distinct from P10 S5 “reduce the visibility of `pub` items” (narrowing
Rust's `pub(crate)`).

**Why it must be completed before P4 as a whole**: 029g's deletion surface overlaps the rewrite
surfaces of all four refactoring phases. Reversing the order means redoing the same deletions and
baseline updates on the new grammar / new checker layout / new SSA IR.

| 029g deletion surface                                               | File                                                                                                               | Rewritten by which phase                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `KwPub` and syntax branches                                         | `lexer/{tokens,state,mod}.rs`; `parser/parser_state.rs`, `statements/{declarations,imports,functions,bindings}.rs` | **P8** (8.2 lexer convergence / 8.3 Pratt precedence convergence / 8.7 split `parse_assign_after_target`)                                                                                                                                                     |
| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                       | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 AST dead variants** + P8 + D1 directory rename (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                              |
| `auto_bind_to_type` and the `pub` branch of `collect_exports`       | `typecheck/checker.rs`, `environment.rs`                                                                           | **P5** (`include!`→real `mod` and checker splitting are **pure moves**, and the `pub` branch will be moved verbatim into the new files)                                                                                                                       |
| Dead-code exemptions `exempt_pub` / `is_exported` and role dispatch | `typecheck/passes/dead_code.rs`, `module/orchestrator.rs` (inside `check_project`)                                 | **P4 4.2.2** (`check_project` slimming)                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `semantic_tokens` `Public` modifier                                 | `typecheck/checker/semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                             | **P4 4.2.6** + P5 + 4.6 (D55)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `ir_gen` ignores `is_pub` when binding                              | `middle/core/ir_gen.rs`                                                                                            | **P7** (`ir_gen.rs` SSA conversion)                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| 31 `pub` occurrences under `src/std/`                               | `std/list.yx` / `json.yx` / `option.yx` / `result.yx`                                                              | No phase changes these directly, but **P6's hard acceptance requires zero difference under `src/std/` (`git diff --stat src/std/` is empty; the `tests/` direct-driver exception is described in P6's hard-acceptance section)**—they can only land before P6 |

**Incidental benefit**: 029g removes the dead `env.exports` table (written by the producer and
consumed nowhere in the repository) and the `is_exported`/`is_visible` accessors ⇒ P4's 4.3
obligation ledger loses one more “produced but never consumed” field.

| 029g.7 Documentation         | 029g.7.1 Language reference and guide                                                                                        | `reference/language-spec/{modules,syntax,language-overview}.md`, `warning-code/warning-codes.md`, `guide/modules.md` | The specification no longer contains statements contradicting the implementation by saying “pub can still be written”; the “pub never triggers W1001” statement in `warning-codes.md` is corrected as well |

**Acceptance (behavior changes; red criterion first)**:

1. **Red first, then green**: each of the two behavior changes must first land a red criterion
   before code changes—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② an unreferenced
   top-level binding in the Lib/Script role newly reports W1001 (previously `pub` items were
   absolutely exempt).
2. **The test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` case in
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixture, they must be replaced with
   equivalent new cases.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (a new parse error + a new W1001) →
   update the corpus differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG in
   the same commit; the IR snapshot is expected to have a zero diff, and any non-zero diff must be
   explained.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with another phase (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` all pass.

**Ordering**: It overlaps 3.4 in files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must be serial and
cannot run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g track does not
depend on 3.4; implementers may choose which to start based on the context at hand.

> **Commit correspondence (2026-10-08)**: This section's incorporation (the P3.5 chapter +
> main-chain/constraint rows) and RFC-039's D56 were incorporated together during the workspace
> cleanup of parallel streams in `97071c81b`—that commit's message records “3.4 supplement
> registration + D57/D58 decision filing” and does not mention this track. History is not rewritten;
> following the existing convention (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 landing note), it is
> registered in place as evidence for later bisecting.

Minimal reproduction: `lib.yx` defines `Point.scale_by: (self: &Point, k: Float) -> Float`, and `main.yx` contains `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` ⇒ E1014, while `p.scale_by(2.0)` ⇒ 6.0. **D59 classification: Category C** (old behavior was not successful: named arguments were silently dropped, leading to runtime failure or a silently wrong value). **Scope (final form after two narrowing rounds on 2026-11-26—only three additions; everything else is deletion and registration)**: ① `AstToIrGenerator::method_param_info` (`src/middle/lower/query.rs`)—use the definition-unit qualified name `{module}.{Type}.{method}[#N]` to obtain declared formal-parameter names from the sole cross-unit carrier `ModuleInfo::method_overloads` (the candidate ↔ mixed-IR name ↔ formal-name vectors have the same order and share the same source as the typecheck injection surface); the call site (`src/middle/lower/expr/call.rs`) uses `method_dispatch_name`'s qualified name to look up the name table rather than using two bare names. These two locations fix **only** cross-unit methods with a **bare-name import** (`local == target`); the candidate injection surface retains the pre-4.9.9 narrowing rule (`local != target` is skipped), so named arguments on alias imports are outside the fix scope (see “Known Gaps”). ② `ModuleRegistry::all_method_bindings` (`src/frontend/module/registry.rs`) merges by **ascending module key**—**Category C (independent of the original bug): eliminate “multiple results for the same input” caused by HashMap iteration order**, rather than fixing the original bug; criterion = same-file unit test `test_all_method_bindings_merge_is_deterministic_across_hash_seeds` (32 registry instances with alternating insertion orders; only one single binding is allowed per method key; removing ascending-key merging produces two results). **Criterion (red first, then green)**: 2 driver-level tests in `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` (bare import with one candidate 6.0 / two candidates selected by name 6.0 and 30, all with value assertions; the file header records the pathology gate); unit tests in `src/middle/lower/tests/query.rs` (`method_param_info` empty-name-table guard ⇒ None, with a positive control that returns the non-empty table unchanged); unit test in `src/frontend/module/registry.rs` (the deterministic criterion above). Project-level fixture `tests/yaoxiang-multifile/named-args-cross-unit-method` (the `alias-overload` fixture is deleted along with retirement of the alias surface); the corpus differential baseline `tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl` now has 404 lines: **relative to the direct parent commit `ac810e97`, 405→404** (an intermediate state once contained `alias-overload`); **relative to the pre-4.9.9 baseline `08ccacc5`, 403→404** (+1 base fixture `named-args-cross-unit-method`; `alias-overload` never entered the final history). The line-count change = an unavoidable result of fixtures entering and leaving (`corpus_probe` regeneration is byte-for-byte identical to the committed baseline), **not lost coverage**. **Known Gaps (each named explicitly; old behavior = silently ignored or silently discarded; D60② should report but does not, Category A)**: closure-value binding / block-body function declaration / named nested function declaration / built-in container constructors other than `len` named arguments / whole-module import / RFC-004 binding arm. **Two of these are corrected according to P0 measurements**: ① the **static-function shape** (both this unit and cross-unit, both definition and binding forms) is **entirely unavailable today**—this unit's `check` reports E3006, a cross-unit definition-form `run` reports E6007, and a cross-unit binding-form `run` reports E6006; positional and named arguments produce the same code, which is unrelated to named arguments and is not “named arguments being silently discarded”; ② **RFC-004 cross-unit positional arguments fail in the same way** (`check` passes, `run` reports E6006), with the root cause being that the dispatch name is absent from the merged function table, again unrelated to named arguments. **Fixed (4.9.10-S2b, D59 Category C fixed in passing: old E6007/E1014 behavior was unsuccessful, and no previously successful program becomes unsuccessful)**: ① **alias-import named arguments** (`use a.{Temp as X}` + `t.bump(k = 2.0)`); ② **namespace arm** (named arguments after `lib.Temp(..)`); ③ **inferred-receiver named arguments** (the receiver type is inferred and has no written annotation). |                                            | 4.9.10 Cross-unit method identity is undefined (registered 2026-11-25; confirmed as a structural problem during 4.9.9 implementation): the method-candidate key `{Type}.{method}` does not contain module qualification, so for same-named types across modules, three consumers—candidate injection (`driver::arms::visible_method_overloads`), typecheck's formal-name/candidate matching, and IR dispatch (`method_dispatch_name`)—each guess the provider by name, and a change to any one of them moves the “silent wrong value” to another one. **Root-cause solution**: upgrade type identity to **module-qualified identity** (`{module}.{Type}`), and change the method-candidate key to `{module}.{Type}.{method}`; one location resolves it and three locations only read it. `collect_used_in_type` must not change)

- [x] **5.2 Extract `refinement`** (2 level-3 tasks)
- [x] **5.3 Extract `annotations`** (2 level-3 tasks)

| Level 2                     | Level 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Prerequisite | Acceptance                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 5.1 `include!` → real `mod` | 5.1.1 Replace the `include!` at the end of `checker.rs` with real `mod` declarations (do not hard-code line anchors; it was measured at the end of the file at the time)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | P4 complete  | C1 zero-diff; `semantic_tokens.rs` gains module identity                                                                               |
|                             | 5.1.2 Add `use super::*` or individual imports (the `include!` era implicitly inherited the scope)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | 5.1.1        | `cargo build` passes                                                                                                                   |
| 5.2 Extract `refinement`    | 5.2.1 Move out the refinement blocks (three non-contiguous sections of the original `checker.rs`; now the single file `checker/refinement.rs`, containing `ReturnRefinement` / `RefinedWalkCtx`), leaving the retained surface and six cross-boundary shared items in place                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | 5.1.1        | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                           |
|                             | 5.2.2 Converge the refinement entry point on “`&self` + return diagnostics” and **do not detach it from `impl`**: `collect_refined_binding_checks` (now `checker/refinement.rs`, `pub(super)`) no longer implicitly writes the error channel through `&mut self`; the diagnostic set is returned upward and written at the sole call site `check_module_impl` (`checker.rs`, symbol location). **Reason for retaining `impl`**: the only field in this family is `self.env` (technically detaching `impl` would be feasible), but converting the entry point and traversal to free functions would also move the call sites: `resolve_type_annotation` has 8 producers (6 annotation paths + `refined_walk_stmt` + `collect_refined_var_names_in_stmt`), `collect_param_refinements` has 2 producers + 1 test, and this would create a reverse dependency from the “retained surface (signature collection) → refinement”—contrary to the coupling-removal intent of this step | 5.2.1        | —                                                                                                                                      |
| 5.3 Extract `annotations`   | 5.3.1 Move out the annotation-validation family of 10 items (now the single file `checker/annotations.rs`; `check_annotation_type_names` is the `pub(super)` entry point, the other 9 items are private to the family, and `is_predicate_head` is a free function within the family)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | 5.2.2        | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                           |
|                             | 5.3.2 **`collect_used_in_type` (`pub(crate)`) remains `pub(crate)` and under the `checker` module path**: it is a **shared-surface** function (consumed by both `collect_function_signature` and `inference/statements.rs:16`), and measurement shows that 5.3.1 **did not migrate it** ⇒ the “zero caller changes” criterion **was already satisfied**; therefore, **do not add** a new `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export. **Constraint retained**: if it is migrated with the family in the future (into annotations or another later batch), `checker.rs` must add a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the import remains unchanged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | 5.3.1        | **“Zero caller changes” is this step's hard acceptance criterion: `git diff src/frontend/core/sema/inference/statements.rs` is empty** |

**Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is migrated with the annotation family in the future, **then** `checker.rs` must
add a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the import remains unchanged; measurement
shows that 5.3 **did not migrate it**, so this batch added no re-export (the criterion was already
satisfied).

**Only split confirmed large blocks.** Do not split modules of only 200–400 lines—this increases
navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and yields zero decoupling benefit. The remaining submodules
(signatures / type_defs / imports) are to be split only after the files grow back to 1,500 lines.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (First-Principles Rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: The end state of D62 is a **unified term world**—type positions and value positions
> share one set of compile-time terms. One strength declaration produces one quantifier reading
> `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`; `q` is the **sole input** to slot allocation, and the call-site actual view and
> implementation-head binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equality is a **pure
> determination** (identical after normalizing both sides; it does not bind type variables);
> evidence is the **sole entry point** for q=0 slots (four sources: literals / value environment /
> single-value pinning / Γ equalities); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of q=0 (it holds for
> both closed and open/recursive terms); Σ construction sites **reuse** the same evidence interface
> rather than establishing another one. **The completion criterion = the invariants hold, not that
> the subphase names have been checked off.**

> **6.9 closure criterion**: I1–I5 and I7 all hold, I6 is closed according to the design-review
> conclusion for 6.9.5 (does not block P7), and I8 has evidence for every slice; all residual items

> landed on 2026-11-19. **Do not substitute “all subphases checked off” for the invariants
> holding.**

> **Partial order (not a serial chain)**: A fact → {A.C3, B.d, C.2, D design}; B kernel → {B.d, C.2,
> D implementation}; C.1 is independent and complete; F4 decision → A.C3; determination-point
> protocol → B.d; design review → D implementation. A.C3 and B.d may run in parallel but require
> file-surface coordination (C3 leans typecheck→mono, while d leans types/solver→sema); C.2 may run
> in parallel with B.d after 6.9.2-B/6.9.3a (it does not depend on defeq); D implementation waits
> for confirmation of the B design package and depends on A (q=0 erasure) and C.1 (dispatch), and
> may depend on the typed exit in 6.9.3. **P7 gate = the A/B/C exits of 6.9; D does not block.**

> **A.C3 prerequisite: F4 decision (A decided on 2026-11-16; measured)**: The old wording
> “`CheckOnly` evidence does not enter the request” is obsolete—`ConstEvidence`/`CheckOnly` have
> been deleted; the current mechanism is that open-term `normalize` returns `Unproven` ⇒ no request
> is created, and the representation layer `GenericArg::Const(ConstExpr)` can already hold `k-1`.
> **The decision was changed to two orthogonal decisions + one terminal subdecision**: D-a
> representation (A: open terms enter `deferred` and are normalized before enqueueing / B: no
> specialization); D-b evaluation point (mono only; C-1's second field and C-2's recovery from IR
> both break the single representation/evaluator, so C-3 = A); **F4-T termination** (naive firing
> pushes the recursion chain into `max_depth` and hits E3005; T-a: instantiate the condition inside
> the term / T-b: bounded firing + fallback to the original at the boundary / T-c: add a termination
> layer or change the specification). **Do this first, then decide; before measurement, “A is
> already implementable” must not be treated as a conclusion.** **User (2026-11-16): D-a=A-closed,
> D-b=C-3, F4-T=T-b, bound=8; C3 implementation is a separate task, and I4 completeness is not
> claimed.**

> **B.d prerequisite: determination-point protocol (not yet written)**: RFC-027 §12.1 requires that
> determination points first use a unified operation; after unified failure, equality may be used,
> but all partial bindings produced by the unification attempt must first be rolled back. The
> implementation must answer: is the entry point an outer wrapper around `solver.unify` or a new
> `decide` layer; may defeq be attempted only when both sides are ground (with no unbound
> variables); what are the snapshot/restoration boundaries and costs; and do unify and defeq share
> one budget or have one each. **Responsibility boundary**: unify remains responsible for
> subtyping/Any/Never; defeq determines equality only and does not take over subtyping;
> bidirectional subtyping must not be treated as equality (RFC-027 §12.1). **Provide the protocol
> and production call graph before writing code**; 6.9.3c's wiring contract was wasted across two
> rounds by assuming `can_assign` was the determination point, while `AssignmentChecker` has zero
> production instantiations.

> **E acceptance and residuals (I8, cross-cutting)**: Every slice must provide ① zero
> corpus/IR-snapshot drift or item-by-item classification; ② `testsuite run fast` + affected
> integration tests; ③ error-code-generator idempotence (if an emission point/code registry
> changes); ④ behavior changes classified under D59 and handled red first, then green. **Wiring
> tasks additionally require**: production call-graph evidence (which production entry point, how
> many paths, which are reachable); single-test reachability must not be used to impersonate user
> reachability; rollback and budget must have measured figures. **Residual disposition**: #537
> (Category D, proof-function formal-parameter refinement silently discarded; not fixed before
> adjudication, and 6.9.4/6.9.5 must not depend on its fix), #539 (import-surface q=0; C-phase
> boundary, and if not closed, 6.9.4 covers only module-internal behavior), #540 (deep-nesting stack
> overflow; **closed**—3.20.30 was closed on 2026-11-14: orchestration-layer 64MB large-stack
> thread + parser depth gate MAX_PARSE_DEPTH=1024 + E0019; see the 3.20.30 row in 09), #541
> (TailCall; **closed**—three sites moved in and out together on 2026-11-16:
> `call_form_is_rewritten` / `replace_calls_in_function` / `drop_erased_call_args` cover
> Call/TailCall through the single-point `rewritten_call_target`; the init section and function body
> share one site-rewriting implementation; red→green + three mutations), #542 (orphaned shared
> layer; **landed (2026-11-19)**: DCE pass + post-mono two entry-point wiring + C2c temporary
> workaround removal; red→green, 402/402, function-table attribution and deviations), #552
> (multi-parameter imported predicate proof execution; 6.9.5 neighborhood, separate case).
> **Ownership awaiting adjudication**: the four open-constraint tripwires (`Eq(N, n)`) in
> `rfc027_refined_transparency` do not belong to 6.9.4's constant-equality bridge; they remain in
> 6.9.4's outOfScope or move to the 6.9.1/E4018 proof-function surface, which requires adjudication.

> **Non-claims / boundaries**: This item covers only record Σ (B: witness field), does not touch
> Π/`DepFn`, and does not claim that Π/Σ are complete; 6.9.4 covers only constant equalities and
> does not deliver the open-constraint `Eq(N,n)` tripwire; the second value position of `f(y)(y)` is
> outside this item; witness erasure ≠ Runtime check erasure; if #537 is not fixed, 6.9.4/6.9.5
> cover only shapes that do not depend on proof-function formal-parameter refinement; if #539 is not
> fixed, 6.9.4 covers only module-internal behavior; #540 is closed (3.20.30); #542 landed
> (2026-11-19); 2.1.4's inner-isolation red state was cleared on 2026-11-20 (the criterion was
> rewritten by slot identity and closed in 2.1.4)⇒ **all prerequisites for promoting `verify` to a
> gate have been removed**.

**Hard acceptance** (**criterion revised on 2026-10-27, carrying forward decision ② of
2026-10-26**): `git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be empty **in every
round of 6.1–6.7**. **Direct-driver test files** under `tests/` (tests that directly drive changed
code, such as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be modified when mechanically required by the
change, but each must be registered with **file / line count / reason**; **tests must not be deleted
and assertions must not be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavior-fix** batch (new
diagnostic code + baseline update), does not fall under this hard acceptance criterion, and is
handled as a separate round with separate adjudication.

> **Revision relationship**: The original criterion (decision ② of 2026-10-26) was written as
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, treating all of `tests/` as a single zero-difference
> requirement; the revised criterion **only changes direct-driver test files from “zero difference”
> to “may be modified but must register file / line count / reason”**, while the **zero-difference
> requirement for the corpus layer (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer (`tests/baselines`), and
> standard library (`src/std/`) remains unchanged**. First application = 6.1.2: only
> `tests/formatter_integration.rs` changed, by **3 lines** (2 occurrences of `assert_format_eq`
> changing `i64`→`Int64` + 1 comment line), because the changed spelling requires the assertion's
> expected type name to be updated; no tests were deleted and no assertions were weakened. See “P6
> 6.1 Name Normalization Closure.”

**Risk**: The precedence table is the sole authority; a missed consumer silently changes
associativity (no error, only a different parse result). The defenses are the permanent D1–D3
assertions and operator-property cross-validation tests; every new operator must enter both the
table and the cross-validation tests.

> back to `sema`, will be blocked by `check-boundary.py`.

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 stop-the-bleeding channel (decision of 2026-10-05)**: P3's prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR
> verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential and performance baseline) may proceed in
> parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding from correctness defects must not be blocked by
> criterion-infrastructure construction; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified
> Driver requires all three criterion layers to be in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every action in P1 (1.2.x adds `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Defect criteria must be **written in red first** (2.4.1/2.4.3) + the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so that red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order causes bugs to become codified as “established behavior” in the phase table                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g's (#399) deletion surface covers the rewrite targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (the list is in §P3.5 of this document)—reversing the order means redoing the same deletions on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` transformation and checker split modify the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| P5 → P6                   | Continuous changes to the same file must be separated; otherwise, regressions cannot be located by bisection                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representations do not converge first, the new IR grows into a third representation; **P7 gate = the phase A/B/C exits of 6.9** (I1–I3, I5, I7; that is, 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and completed 6.9.4), while D (Σ) does not block; P7 may consume only the quantifier-derived views and defeq interface and must not establish a parallel ledger; the 7.0 pure-move batch is a P7 prerequisite, is not subject to this gate, and must not consume the undecided defeq/quantifier interfaces |
| P7/P8 → P9                | 9.5's snapshot baseline and 9.3's `pub(crate)` leak count reach their final form only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

### Parallelization Groups

| Group                                    | Members                                                                            | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only group authorized by RFC)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                            | Disjoint file sets: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs. `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                                 |
| B                                        | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                      | Each independently adds a `mod`; revert file by file                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| C                                        | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                    | The three criterion layers are mutually independent                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| D                                        | 4.4 (proof-layer wrap-up) ∥ the entire P6 line                                     | `02` explicitly states in S5 that it “should proceed independently of S1-S4”                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| E                                        | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | All mutually independent after 4.1                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| F                                        | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced in P0 may be developed in parallel) | 9.5's snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| G                                        | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | Disjoint file sets (verified 2026-10-05: S3 modifies `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 modifies `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 modifies two `pub` occurrences under `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; no pairwise overlap) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (B6/E5
same-batch files); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (same files `checker.rs` /
`environment.rs`—the external track's `pub` deletion batch and the silent-channel fixes must be
serial).

**New internal documentation constraint**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial; 7.0 →
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial (7.0 is P7's pure-move prerequisite batch), and 7b's `Phi` arm must
precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “post-hoc checks,” while rules are
  “pre-hoc judgment.” P9's scripts cannot prevent “patching when a refactor was required”; only
  D0–D4's review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative list of CI scripts**—the three coexisting lists that constituted
  original gap G3 prevented closure. This table merges them into 10 active scripts, each owned by
  one phase (9.8 was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24), with report-only status and hard-failure
  timing explicitly traceable.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to perform after the
  refactoring”**—its deletion surface overlaps the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039 D56).
  Deferring it until after the refactoring means redoing the same deletions over the new grammar,
  new checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as incorporating `2315`/`2341` into 7e and
  incorporating RFC status corrections into S4.
- **P5's steps are supplied by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding the checker split would exceed the granularity at which changes can
  be rolled back.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero caller changes” as its hard acceptance criterion**—the split must be
  independently revertable.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it says only that “the fixed
  defects must not be rolled back,” and lacks a requirement to record what was fixed. **Execution
  convention**: the commit message for every 1.3.x fix must reference the fixed test name and defect
  description as evidence for later bisecting.
- ~~**7b.1 granularity is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b, two
  exclusive commits, per DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 granularity is too coarse**—approximately 89 references are renamed; a missed change
  **silently changes associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding level-3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as 7e.1,
  and D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34 opcode reclamation was incorporated into 7e.1, with
  deletion left to P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally assigned to “separate issues”**~~
  **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated as 7e.2 / 7e.3. The exception table (throw/try) is core
  language semantics and must not be left for future implementation.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**:
  incorporated into P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated
  into the generation-time gate task in P10 S6.

## Conflict Registration: All Adjudicated

> **The original “Conflict Registration” C1–C8 and the open questions in each document have all
> converged into the [RFC-039 Decision Register](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md)
> (D1–D50).** This document retains no pending items. Item-by-item correspondence:

| Original ID | Issue                                                                               | Decision                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| C1          | `precedence_inline.rs` is revived in P1 and deleted in P8                           | **Revive** (P1's prerequisite is that the test contains genuine assertions); P8 no longer deletes the file (Pratt is retained)                                                                  |
| C2          | “Grammar-driven” commitment vs. table lookup                                        | **Fallback approach**: retain Pratt + a single declarative precedence table + cross-validation of the two `BinOp` implementations from one source (the LALRPOP route was withdrawn), see P8 8.3 |
| C3          | Conflict between the C6 category definition and S1 classification                   | **S1 is classified under C6** (revival does not require equivalence criteria, only regression tests); the C6 definition is expanded to “pure deletion or pure revival”                          |
| C4          | `test_release_plan_spans_consumed` whitelist                                        | **No whitelist**; the difference set must be empty; if it cannot be empty, the `ReleasePlan` contract is defective → change to `PlanId` (D20/D41)                                               |
| C5          | Internal differences between the two `Aggregation` functions have not been verified | **P4's 4.2.7 explicitly lists this as a mandatory verification item**; confirm line by line during implementation                                                                               |
| C6          | The wasm playground fix requires P4's `ProgramKind`                                 | **The wasm-path defect fix is incorporated into 4.2.8**; P3 handles only the three native entry points                                                                                          |
| C7          | Ownership of `method_def_ordinals`                                                  | **Assigned to 04** (P7 batch c), see D21                                                                                                                                                        |
| C8          | `upvalue_count` correction and the `.42` version number                             | **Fix + raise `VERSION` from 4 to 5** (the format header already has `MAGIC` + `VERSION` fields, `codegen/bytecode.rs:14-16`), see D17                                                          |
